questions.stem: \(ABCD\) is a square of side length \(6\) metres and \(EFGC\) is a rectangle, with \(D\), \(C\), \(G\) collinear and \(EF=BE=x\) metres. The composite area is \(223\text{ m}^2\).

parts.stem: Create a quadratic equation relating the area of the composite shape to \(x\).
parts.hint: The rectangle \(EFGC\) has width \(EF=x\) and height \(CE=CB+BE=6+x\). Add its area to the square's area.

steps.explain: The rectangle \(EFGC\) has width \(EF=x\) and height \(CE=CB+BE=6+x\) (since \(CB\) is a side of the square).
The square has area \(6^2=36\text{ m}^2\). Add the two areas and set the total equal to \(223\).

questions.stem: The area of a parallelogram is \(70 \text{ cm}^2\). The length of its base is \(4 \text{ cm}\) longer than twice its perpendicular height. Let \(x\) be the perpendicular height. Find the length of the base.

steps.explain: The base is \(4\text{ cm}\) longer than twice the perpendicular height \(x\), so the base is \(2x + 4\).

questions.stem: In the diagram below, \(ABCD\) is a rectangle in which \(AB = 21 \text{ cm}\). The square \(AXYD\) is removed and the remaining rectangle has an area of \(80 \text{ cm}^2\). Let \(x\) be the length of \(BC\). Calculate all the possible lengths of \(BC\).

steps.explain: Since \(AXYD\) is a square and \(BC = AD = x\), the side lengths of the square are \(x\). So, \(AX = x\).
The length of \(XB\) is the total length \(AB\) minus \(AX\).
The remaining rectangle \(XBCY\) has dimensions \(x\) by \((21 - x)\). Set up the area equation.
Expand and rearrange into a standard quadratic equation.

questions.stem: Solve the following equation by making an appropriate substitution: \(x^{2/3} = 7x^{1/3} - 12\)

steps.explain: Notice that \(x^{2/3} = (x^{1/3})^2\). This means the equation is "hiding" a quadratic — make the substitution \(u = x^{1/3}\) to turn it into a standard quadratic in \(u\).
Rewrite the original equation in terms of \(u\) and rearrange into standard quadratic form.
Factorise: find two numbers that multiply to \(12\) and add to \(-7\) — these are \(-3\) and \(-4\).
Substitute back \(x^{1/3}\) for \(u\) and cube both sides to solve for \(x\).
Solve for the second value the same way.

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes the sketch of the parabola $y = x^2 - 2x - 8$?
options: Opens upwards, passes through $(2,0)$ and $(4,0)$, y-intercept at $(0,8)$, vertex at $(3,-2)$
Opens downwards, passes through $(-2,0)$ and $(4,0)$, y-intercept at $(0,-8)$, vertex at $(1,-9)$
Opens upwards, passes through $(-4,0)$ and $(2,0)$, y-intercept at $(0,8)$, vertex at $(-1,9)$
Opens upwards, passes through $(-2,0)$ and $(4,0)$, y-intercept at $(0,-8)$, vertex at $(1,-9)$

steps.explain: The coefficient of $x^2$ in $y=x^2-2x-8$ is $+1$ (positive), so the parabola opens **upwards** (concave up) — this immediately rules out any "opens downwards" option.

topics.title: Solving quadratic equations by completing the square

questions.stem: Solve the following quadratic equation using completing the square: \(x^2 - 6x - 2 = 0\)

steps.explain: Move the constant term to the right side.
Add the square of half the \(x\) coefficient to both sides. \((-3)^2 = 9\).
Factor the perfect square and simplify.
Take the square root of both sides.
